<div id="contributing" class="section">

# Contributing<a href="#contributing" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Everyone interacting with and contributing to pip-tools is expected to
follow the
<a href="https://github.com/pypa/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md"
class="reference external">PSF Code of Conduct</a>.

<div id="project-contribution-guidelines" class="section">

## Project Contribution Guidelines<a href="#project-contribution-guidelines" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Here are a few additional or emphasized guidelines to follow when
contributing to <span class="pre">`pip-tools`</span>:

- If you need to have a virtualenv outside of
  <span class="pre">`tox`</span>, it is possible to reuse its
  configuration to provision it with
  <a href="https://tox.wiki/en/latest/reference/cli.html#tox-devenv-(d)"
  class="reference external">tox devenv</a>.

- Always provide tests for your changes and run
  <span class="pre">`tox`</span>` `<span class="pre">`-p`</span>` `<span class="pre">`all`</span>
  to make sure they are passing the checks locally.

- Give a clear one-line description in the PR (that the maintainers can
  add to <a href="#./CHANGELOG.md" class="reference internal"><span
  class="xref myst">CHANGELOG</span></a> afterwards).

- Wait for the review of at least one other contributor before merging.

- Before merging, assign the PR to a milestone for a version to help
  with the release process.

The only exception to those guidelines is for trivial changes, such as
documentation corrections or contributions that do not change pip-tools
itself.

Contributions following these guidelines are always welcomed, encouraged
and appreciated.

<div id="llm-generated-contributions" class="section">

### LLM Generated Contributions<a href="#llm-generated-contributions" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Contributors are free to use whatever tools they like, but we have some
additional guidance for LLM-assisted contributions.

When interacting in pip-tools spaces (issues, pull requests, matrix,
discord, etc.), do not use LLMs to speak for you, except for translation
or grammar edits. This includes the creation of changelogs and PR
descriptions. Human-to-human communication is foundational to open
source communities.

<div class="admonition caution">

Caution

In extreme cases, low quality PRs may be closed as spam.

</div>

<div id="responsibility" class="section">

#### Responsibility<a href="#responsibility" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Remember that you, not the LLM, are responsible for your contributions.
Be ready to discuss your changes. Do not submit code you have not
reviewed.

Do your best to follow the conventions and standards of the project.
Make sure your code really works. Be thoughtful about testing and
documentation.

Try to make your code brief, and recognize when less is more.

</div>

<div id="autonomous-code-submissions" class="section">

#### Autonomous Code Submissions<a href="#autonomous-code-submissions" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

The use of agents which write code and submit pull requests without
human review is not permitted.

</div>

<div id="pull-request-templates" class="section">

#### Pull Request Templates<a href="#pull-request-templates" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Please do not replace the pull request template, which is part of the
maintainers’ process.

</div>

</div>

<div id="the-good-first-issue-label" class="section">

### The <span class="pre">`good`</span>` `<span class="pre">`first`</span>` `<span class="pre">`issue`</span> label<a href="#the-good-first-issue-label" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

The <a
href="https://github.com/pypa/pip-tools/labels/good%20first%20issue%22"
class="reference external"><span class="pre"><code
class="docutils literal notranslate">good</code></span><code
class="docutils literal notranslate"> </code><span class="pre"><code
class="docutils literal notranslate">first</code></span><code
class="docutils literal notranslate"> </code><span class="pre"><code
class="docutils literal notranslate">issue</code></span> label</a> is
used to designate items which are being left for new contributors.
They’re a great way to get onboarded into the project and learn.

Having an LLM resolve one of these issues does not help anyone learn.
Therefore, please be considerate of those who may benefit from these
opportunities, and refrain from asking an LLM to produce a complete
solution.

</div>

</div>

<div id="project-release-process" class="section">

## Project Release Process<a href="#project-release-process" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Releases require approval by a member of the
<a href="https://github.com/orgs/pypa/teams/pip-tools-admins"
class="reference external"><span class="pre"><code
class="docutils literal notranslate">pip-tools-admins</code></span>
team</a>.

Commands given below may assume that your fork is named
<span class="pre">`origin`</span> in git remotes and the main repo is
named <span class="pre">`upstream`</span>.

This is the current release process:

- Create a branch for the release. *e.g.,
  <span class="pre">`release/v3.4.0`</span>*.

- Use <span class="pre">`towncrier`</span> to update the
  <a href="#./CHANGELOG.md" class="reference internal"><span
  class="xref myst">CHANGELOG</span></a>, *e.g.,
  <span class="pre">`towncrier`</span>` `<span class="pre">`build`</span>` `<span class="pre">`--version`</span>` `<span class="pre">`v3.4.0`</span>*.

- Push the branch to your fork, *e.g.,
  <span class="pre">`git`</span>` `<span class="pre">`push`</span>` `<span class="pre">`-u`</span>` `<span class="pre">`origin`</span>` `<span class="pre">`release/v3.4.0`</span>*,
  and create a pull request.

- Merge the pull request after the changes are approved.

- Make sure that the tests/CI still pass.

- Fetch the latest changes to <span class="pre">`main`</span> locally.

- Create an unsigned tag with the release version number prefixed with a
  <span class="pre">`v`</span>, *e.g.,
  <span class="pre">`git`</span>` `<span class="pre">`tag`</span>` `<span class="pre">`-a`</span>` `<span class="pre">`v3.4.0`</span>` `<span class="pre">`-m`</span>` `<span class="pre">`v3.4.0`</span>*,
  and push it to <span class="pre">`upstream`</span>.

- Create a GitHub Release, populated with a copy of the changelog and
  set to “Create a discussion for this release” in the
  <span class="pre">`Announcements`</span> category. Some of the
  markdown will need to be reformatted into GFM. The release title and
  tag should be the newly created tag.

- The <a
  href="https://github.com/pypa/pip-tools/actions/workflows/release.yml"
  class="reference external">GitHub Release Workflow</a> will trigger
  off of the release to publish to PyPI. A member of the
  \[<span class="pre">`pip-tools-leads`</span> team\] must approve the
  publication step.

- Once the release to PyPI is confirmed, close the milestone.

- Publish any release notifications, *e.g., pip-tools matrix channel,
  discuss.python.org, bluesky, mastodon, pypa Discord*.

</div>

<div id="adding-change-notes-with-prs" class="section">

## Adding Change Notes with PRs<a href="#adding-change-notes-with-prs" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

It is important to maintain a changelog to explain to users what changed
between versions.

To avoid merge conflicts, we use
<a href="https://towncrier.readthedocs.io/en/stable/"
class="reference external">Towncrier</a> to maintain our changelog.

Towncrier uses separate files, “news fragments”, for each pull request.
On release, those fragments are compiled into the changelog.

You don’t need to install Towncrier to contribute, you just have to
follow some simple rules!

- In your pull request, add a new file into
  <span class="pre">`changelog.d/`</span> with a filename formatted as
  <span class="pre">`$NUMBER.$CATEGORY.md`</span>.

  - The number is the PR number or issue number which your PR addresses.

  - The category is <span class="pre">`bugfix`</span>,
    <span class="pre">`feature`</span>,
    <span class="pre">`deprecation`</span>,
    <span class="pre">`breaking`</span>, <span class="pre">`doc`</span>,
    <span class="pre">`packaging`</span>,
    <span class="pre">`contrib`</span>, or
    <span class="pre">`misc`</span>. The maintainers may use special
    categories <span class="pre">`highlights`</span> and
    <span class="pre">`afterword`</span>, but regular contributors don’t
    generally need to.

  - For example, if your PR fixes bug \#404, the change notes should be
    named <span class="pre">`changelog.d/404.bugfix.md`</span>.

- If multiple issues are addressed, create a symlink to the change notes
  with another issue number in the name. Towncrier will automatically
  merge files into one entry with multiple links.

- Prefer the simple past or constructions with “now”.

- Include a byline,
  <span class="pre">`--`</span>` `<span class="pre">`by`</span>` `<span class="pre">`` {user}`github-username` ``</span>

You can preview the changelog by running
<span class="pre">`tox`</span>` `<span class="pre">`run`</span>` `<span class="pre">`-e`</span>` `<span class="pre">`build-docs`</span>
and viewing the changelog in the docs.

<div id="categories" class="section">

### Categories<a href="#categories" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

The categories for change notes are defined as follows.

- <span class="pre">`bugfix`</span>: A fix for something we deemed
  improper or undesired behavior.

- <span class="pre">`feature`</span>: A new behavior, such as a new flag
  or environment variable.

- <span class="pre">`deprecation`</span>: A declaration of future
  removals and breaking changes in behavior.

- <span class="pre">`breaking`</span>: A change in behavior which
  changes or violates established user expectations (e.g., removing a
  flag or changing output formatting).

- <span class="pre">`doc`</span>: Notable updates to the documentation
  structure or build process.

- <span class="pre">`packaging`</span>: Changes in how
  <span class="pre">`pip-tools`</span> itself is packaged and tested
  which may impact downstreams and redistributors.

- <span class="pre">`contrib`</span>: Changes to the contributor
  experience (e.g., running tests, building the docs, or setting up a
  development environment).

- <span class="pre">`misc`</span>: Changes that don’t fit any of the
  other categories.

- <span class="pre">`highlights`</span>: A prelude to the release notes.
  Normally filled out by the maintainers with important announcements
  concerning a <span class="pre">`pip-tools`</span> release. It is
  rendered before the normal change log categories.

  <div class="admonition important">

  Important

  The file name must not reference a number but be orphan, starting with
  a <span class="pre">`+`</span>.

  </div>

- <span class="pre">`afterword`</span>: A concluding paragraph after the
  release notes. May be filled out by the maintainers if they want to
  include additional free-form notes. It is rendered after the normal
  change log categories.

  <div class="admonition important">

  Important

  The file name must not reference a number but be orphan, starting with
  a <span class="pre">`+`</span>.

  </div>

Sometimes it’s not clear which category to use for a change. Do your
best and a maintainer can discuss this with you during review.

</div>

<div id="examples" class="section">

### Examples<a href="#examples" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Example bugfix, <a href="https://github.com/pypa/pip-tools/pull/2224"
class="reference external"><span class="pre"><code
class="docutils literal notranslate">2223.bugfix.md</code></span></a>:

<div class="highlight-md notranslate">

<div class="highlight">

    Fixed a bug which removed slashes from URLs in `-r` and `-c` in the output
    of `pip-compile` -- by {user}`sirosen`.

</div>

</div>

Example contributor update,
<a href="https://github.com/pypa/pip-tools/pull/2214"
class="reference external"><span class="pre"><code
class="docutils literal notranslate">2214.contrib.md</code></span></a>:

<div class="highlight-md notranslate">

<div class="highlight">

    `pip-tools` now tests on and officially supports `pip` version 25.2
    -- by {user}`sirosen`.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div id="rationale" class="section">

### Rationale<a href="#rationale" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

When making a change to <span class="pre">`pip-tools`</span>, it is
important to communicate the differences that end-users will experience
in a manner that they can understand.

Details of the change that are primarily of interest only to
<span class="pre">`pip-tools`</span> developers may be irrelevant to
most users, and if so, then those details can be omitted from the change
notes. Then, when the maintainers publish a new release, they’ll
automatically use these records to compose a change log for the
respective version.

We write change notes in the past tense because this suits the users who
will be reading these notes. Combined with others, the notes will be a
part of the “news digest” telling the readers what **changed** in a
specific version of <span class="pre">`pip-tools`</span> since the
previous version.

This methodology has several benefits, including those covered by the
<a href="https://towncrier.readthedocs.io/en/stable/#philosophy"
class="reference external">Towncrier Philosophy</a>:

- Change notes separate the user-facing description of changes from the
  implementation details. Details go into the git history, but users
  aren’t expected to care about them.

- The release engineer may not have been involved in each issue and pull
  request. Writing the notes early in the process involves the
  developers in the best position to write good notes.

- Describing a change can help during code review. The reviewer can
  better identify which effects of a change were intentional and which
  were not.

</div>
